Polysomnography Report
Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.

This was a technically adequate overnight diagnostic polysomnogram. Total sleep time was 345 minutes with a sleep efficiency of 82%. Sleep architecture was abnormal due to significant sleep fragmentation. REM sleep was reduced, comprising only 10% of total sleep time.

Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. These events were predominantly obstructive apneas and hypopneas, and they were more severe during REM sleep. This was associated with significant oxygen desaturation, with a nadir SpO2 of 78%. The patient's baseline oxygen saturation was 95%. No significant periodic limb movements were noted.

Impression: The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis.
Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm.
Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
CD15: Positive
PAX5: Positive (dim)
CD45: Negative
CD20: Negative
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.

The patient is a 22-year-old male who presented for a routine skin examination.
He noted a mole on his upper back that he believes has become slightly darker
over the past year. He denies any symptoms of pain or itching associated with the
lesion. He has a history of significant sun exposure during his teen years and
reports occasional sunburns.
PROCEDURES:
Shave Biopsy Upper Back: A 5mm pigmented macule was identified on the
superior aspect of the right scapula. After obtaining consent, the area was
anesthetized with 1% lidocaine with epinephrine and a deep shave biopsy of the
lesion was performed. Hemostasis was achieved with aluminum chloride. The
specimen was sent for histopathologic examination.
IMPRESSION:
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION: Sections show a symmetric, well-circumscribed
proliferation of nested and single melanocytes confined to the dermal-epidermal
junction. The melanocytes are uniform in size and shape with no significant
cytologic atypia. No mitotic activity or ulceration is identified.
DIAGNOSIS: Junctional melanocytic nevus, benign.
